note: balanceConfig — every number of MANO SURVIVOR in one place: difficulty per chapter, the chapter timeline, enemies, drops, rewards, chests, grades, fusion, coin stats and in-run upgrades. Starting values for experiments, tuned with bots (scripts/survivor-balance.mjs, survivor-campaign.mjs); not measured with people.

logicalArena.note: the mobile game's field (360 × 640 screen, portrait): balls bounce and Mano stops at bounds; the PC game has its own (logicalArenaPc)

logicalArenaPc.note: the PC game's field: larger than its screen (1152 × 648 logical, ui.json → pc), about 1.45× its play area each way; the camera follows Mano over it. view: the screen's play area (1152 × 648 minus ui.json → pc.inset): monsters come in at its edges and stay in it, and the balls bounce off it, as on the phone, where the view is the whole field. Mano walks the whole field. spawnBox: monsters come in on the edge of this box around Mano (inside the view) — the phone field's area, so they come as near and as thick as on the phone though the PC screen holds about 3.4× as much; see scripts/survivor-platform-parity.mjs.

xp.note: next = round(previous × growth + add). Experience left lying flies to Mano by itself after pullAfter seconds

overtime.note: the chapter is cleared only when the boss falls. Past 240 s with the boss alive the fight goes on (boss overtime): every 30 s monsters come 15% faster; and monsters (and the boss) hit hitsHarder× harder every 30 s, so a run that can no longer win ends

mobSpeed.note: and the ordinary monsters run faster the longer the chapter's boss lives: from `after` s after it came, ×(1 + step) more every `every` s, never past ×max (a step of the clock, not of each frame); back to ×1 the moment it falls, and every run starts at ×1. Elites and bosses keep their own speed

chapter.packNote: each spawn is a pack: `pack` monsters of one kind together at one point of the edge, every `spawnInterval` s (fewer if the screen is near enemySoftLimit). Monster HP climbs steeply through the chapter (hpMultiplier) because Mano's in-run upgrades multiply

beyondLastChapter.note: each chapter past the list multiplies the last one by these

rewards.note: every coin of chapter N (rewards, coins on the field, coins in its chests) is worth coinGrowth^(N−1), times the coin stat — the same pace as the monsters' HP past chapter 5. First clear with both elites = 8 chests, a repeat clear = 6

chest.note: only weapons that can really be played are rolled (today: the bouncy ball, one roll per chest plus coins)

fusion.note: three of the same weapon and grade make one of the next grade; EX cannot be fused

perma.note: each stat has its own level L (from 0): value × mul^L (or + add × L); next price = floor(price × priceGrowth^L). Caps here are game rules for permanent stats, shown in the shop.

upgrades.note: in-run only, reset after every run; no cap and no hidden slow-down. The core four: balls per volley ×2, gap between volleys ×0.7, damage ×1.5, bounce limit ×2

catSwap.note: in a run with the cats, the magnet card's place in the pool goes to 냥냥 연금술 (same number of cards, same equal chance); it leaves the pool at its last level

upgrades.catCards: friendCats' cards (friends.js): in runs with the cats all five join the pool (same equal chance as every card); 뚱냥이, 스피드냥이, 빠르게 할퀴기 and 발톱 갈기 only once there is a cat. They change the cats only; the ball's cards change the ball only. 친구냥이 +1 cat; 뚱냥이 size ×mul, hit area ×rangeMul; 스피드냥이 speed ×mul; 빠르게 할퀴기 gap ×mul; 발톱 갈기 damage ×mul.

performance.ballBudgetNote: at most this many balls fly at once; a volley that would pass it fires fewer balls, each carrying the damage of those it stands for (the total never drops)

cats.note: Cat companions (단추·호두·모루). They join for good with chapter 5's first clear (story.json → rewards.forest, with one S-grade red ball and the rerolls, once) and come along from activeFromChapter on. They gather coins and experience lying on the field (each its own pick, all three on different ones; everything within `magnet` of a cat flies to it, so a pile goes in one sweep), never fight, never get hurt and never block Mano. Hearts they only take with 냥냥 연금술. The fighting cats are another thing: friendCats.

rerolls.note: redraws of the upgrade cards (chapter 5's reward opens them: story.json → rewards.forest.rerolls a run). From fromChapter on every run starts with that many; a redraw puts the three cards on show back and draws three others the same way (equal chances; other than those shown while the pool has enough).

friendCats.note: 친구냥이 (friends.js): fighting cats in runs with the cats. Each 친구냥이 card brings one more (+1). One scratch = catBase × 발톱 갈기, where catBase = the ball's damage at the start of the run (base × grade × coin stat 공격 피해) × damageCoef; Mano's 치명타 확률 and 치명타 피해 apply. The gap between scratches = interval × the coin stat 공격 주기 × 빠르게 할퀴기. The scratch hits every monster in a circle of radius swipe at reach in front of the cat (뚱냥이 grows both, and the cat's size up to maxDrawScale as drawn). speed: px/s; leash: how far from Mano a cat goes after monsters (on screen only); seekEvery: s between looks for a nearer target; crowdPenalty: px a monster counts further for each cat already on it; stickiness: px nearer another must be to change targets; attackSeconds: the scratch's length (shorter, down to minAttackSeconds, when the gap is shorter), strikeAt: its share where the claw lands; recoverSeconds: the paw coming back (drawn); firstScratch: the most a new cat waits; homeRadius: where cats wait near Mano with nothing to fight; powerAt: 발톱 갈기's multiplier from which the scratch is drawn golden; packBonus: every cat beyond the first adds this to every cat's scratch (1 + packBonus × (cats − 1)); drawH: an idle cat's height in field px.

percentHeart.note: a 퍼센트 하트 heals this share of the maximum HP (set per 냥냥 연금술 level). Only cats make them, from a normal heart; they are never turned again and only Mano picks them up.

lateGame.note: From fromChapter on, each phase of the chapter (same order as chapter.phases) multiplies the monsters' HP and their hits on top of everything else, so the middle and the end of a run stay a fight; elites and the boss get specialHp, each its own (the thief comes early, at 70 s, and must be catchable in its 30 s, so it gets no extra). It comes in step by step: a little at fromChapter, all of it from fullAtChapter on. Chapters before fromChapter are untouched.

writer.note: From Tizzzz's chapter on (she rewrites a card at every level-up, so a run's build ends far stronger than before), each phase of the run multiplies the monsters' HP and hits once more, on top of the push above; mid-boss and boss get specialHp (the thief none, so it stays catchable). Tuned so a bot that takes her edits clears chapter 21 a little less often than it did before she came.

bossGuard.note: From fromChapter on (with Tizzzz: she joins at chapter 15's clear) the skull king loses at most maxShare of its HP each second (burst: seconds' worth that can go at once; damage over that is lost) and hits `hits`× harder (body, charge, slam). With 0.04 a fight lasts at least 25 s however strong the build, and the king can still hurt it. Tuned on bots that pick like a person (the 'human' policy).

tizzzz.note: The writer Tizzzz joins for good with the reward of chapter 15 (story.json → rewards.skulltown, which also grows the red ball to SS). From activeFromChapter on, at every level-up she rewrites one of the three cards at random: that card does its own effect `times` times over (×2 → ×4, ×1.5 → ×2.25, +8%p → +16%p…), exactly as if it had been chosen that many times. A card that cannot take it (a card with levels too close to its last) is never picked; if none can, the cards are left alone.

blessings.note: Battle blessings from the story (story.json → rewards). Temporary balance values. chance: per ball hit; perSecond: at most this many of that blessing in one second however many balls fly (a token bucket, so a screen of balls cannot set it off hundreds of times); seconds: how long it lasts on a monster, a new one only renews it (never stacks). The boss is never frozen: the snow blessing slows it instead. Lightning hits are never a ball hit, so they can never set off more lightning (no chains of chains). final (마왕의 탱탱볼) multiplies every chance.

bossTypes.note: the ordinary bosses (the 145 s mid-boss and the 210 s boss of every chapter; the extra special bosses that come after the boss in some chapters fight their own way: extraBosses): each gets ONE of these when it comes, from a shuffled bag of the four (the next four come in a new shuffle), and keeps it until it falls. A: walks, stops, shows the path and charges along it (its own windup, charge speed and charge hit). B: walks at Mano weaving left and right (weave: the most it turns off her direction, radians; period: s for one weave). C: walks, stops, shows three lanes for aim s, then shoots three shots along them (a fan of spread degrees; each hits like its charge). D: walks; then, shown for warn s (it shakes, a ring round it), runs at mul x its speed for seconds s, turning at most turn rad/s, then walks again. Its HP, hits, reward and when it comes do not change.

extraBosses.note: The extra special bosses (MANO_EXTRA_BOSSES; bosses.js): in the chapters listed, after the chapter's own boss has fallen, one more boss comes, and the chapter is cleared only when it falls too. The field is cleared first (the monsters fade, their attacks go), then intro: calm s of quiet, warn s of WARNING! with a siren and its name and line, appear s of it coming in (Mano cannot be hurt and it cannot be hit until it stands); its fight is in the play area as it was then (box: the PC camera holds still). hpMul: its HP is the chapter boss's (its chapter and late-game strength) × this, never guarded or capped: a strong build ends it quickly. damage: each blow's base, × the boss's hit strength. Attacks (each warned from the start in its real shape, the safe ground shown, blows landing once): ringwave (rings out of it across the whole area, gaps of gapDeg° to stand in, one near Mano), bloom (petal fans from it in turn, skip of them left out), spores (big circles over the area in turn), web (beams across the whole area through it, fire of threads), sweep (a band crossing the whole area, gaps of gap px to stand in, push px/s while inside), rows (every other row of the area), branches (fans from it, every other one), pillars (circles along a fan of rays toward Mano), clock (fans from the area's middle in turn round the dial), chess (rows and columns of a board over the area), combo (parts one after another, after s apart). walk: s between attacks; recover: s after one. phases: the last boss's attack lists by HP share left (above).
extraBosses.blowCapNote: no single blow of an extra boss (its warned shapes or its body) takes more than this share of Mano's full HP (the last boss: its own blowCap), so one mistake is never the end, however strong the chapter's monsters hit
